history.idea: Score the whole document in windows instead of only its first 1500 words, so partly damaged articles are rejected. Split each doc's lowercased words into consecutive 300-word windows over the full length, merging a final window shorter than 100 words into the previous one. For each window, compute the fraction of its word bigrams that are in B. Calibrate a window threshold the same two-fold way as now: build B from 100 target docs, score every window of the other 100, swap, and set tau_w = 0.8 x the 1st percentile of those held-out window scores. Reject a doc if its minimum window score is below tau_w. Keep the existing whole-prefix tau test, but compute it over all words rather than the first 1500. Also apply the non-ASCII-letter check per window: reject if any window has more than 5% of its characters as non-ASCII letters. Run the repetition check on the full word list as now. history.idea: Make the selection fill the token budget T exactly, adaptively, instead of returning whatever the filter keeps. Count tokens per document with tiktoken gpt2 (encode_ordinary_batch) for all docs that pass the non-header guards. Tier 1 = the docs kept now (all current rules, unchanged). Tier 2 = docs that fail ONLY the '= ' header rule but pass every other rule (length, non-ASCII, spam patterns, bigram score >= tau on the first 1500 words, repetition check, dedup against tier 1 and against each other). Also reject from both tiers any doc where under 60% of whitespace-split words are purely alphabetic or punctuation tokens of length <= 20 (base64 or blob junk). Case A, tier 1 tokens >= T: sort tier 1 by bigram score descending, keep the highest-scoring docs until the token sum just reaches T, drop the rest, then shuffle with the seed. Case B, tier 1 tokens < T: keep all of tier 1 and add tier 2 docs in descending bigram-score order until the total reaches T (or tier 2 runs out), then shuffle the union with the seed so the extra docs are interleaved. Never add rejected spam, shuffled or junk docs. Print tier 1 tokens, tier 2 tokens available, tier 2 tokens used, and which case fired.

history.idea:
Keep every current rule and add two conservative whole-document damage checks, applied only to docs that already pass all current rules (before dedup, so a clean copy can still win). 

(a) Tail score: besides the existing bigram score on the first 1500 words, compute the same score (same B, same tau, no new calibration) on the LAST 1500 words of the doc. For docs longer than 3000 words, also score the middle 1500 words. Reject if any of these is below tau.

(b) Tokenizer density: with tiktoken gpt2 encode_ordinary_batch, compute r = tokens / characters over the full text for each target_sample doc and each surviving pool doc. Let lo = 0.9 x min target r and hi = 1.1 x max target r. Reject pool docs with r outside [lo, hi]. This catches character-level scrambling, homoglyphs or blob junk anywhere in the doc.

Safety guard: if the two new checks together remove more than 40% of the tokens the current filter keeps, disable them and return exactly the current selection.

Dedup and the seeded shuffle stay unchanged, and there is no budget filling or score sorting. Print the docs dropped by (a) and by (b), the kept tokens before and after, and whether the guard fired.

history.idea:
Keep every current rule and the current tier-1 selection unchanged, but rescue in-domain articles that fail ONLY the '= ' header rule, using a strict WikiText-format test instead of the loose tau that let web text in during experiments 5 and 6.

1. Format statistic: for a text, split on whitespace and compute p = (number of tokens that are exactly ',' or '.') / (total number of ',' and '.' characters in the text), with p = 0 if there are none. WikiText has spaced punctuation (' , ', ' . ', ' @-@ '), so p is near 1; ordinary web or Q&A text has p near 0.

2. Calibration: compute p for each target_sample doc and set p_min = 0.9 x the 5th percentile. Also take s_q25 = the 25th percentile (not scaled by 0.8) of the two-fold held-out target bigram scores already computed in _calibrate_tau.

3. Rescue tier: a doc that does not start with '= ' is accepted only if all of these hold: p >= p_min; bigram score on its first 1500 words >= s_q25; it passes the existing length, non-ASCII, spam-pattern and repetition checks; it is not a duplicate (same full-text and 300-character-prefix dedup, checked against tier 1 first and then against other rescued docs).

4. Output: union of tier 1 and rescued docs, shuffled once with random.Random(CURATE_SEED). No score sorting, no budget filling, no truncation to T.

5. Safety: if the rescued docs add more than 50% to the tier-1 token estimate, disable the rescue and return exactly the current selection.

Print the number of rescued docs, their token estimate, p_min, s_q25 and whether the safety guard fired.
